2. **AI investments.** Oracle says its AI products may not meet customer needs or may lose to competitors' offerings. If it fails to recoup its AI investment, its business and reputation could suffer. It also flags legal and ethical issues around AI, including bias, lack of transparency, and use of copyrighted or personal data [ORCL chunk 75].

3. **Supply chain.** Some components come from a single vendor. Shortages have also raised production costs that Oracle may not be able to pass on [ORCL chunk 88].

4. **Cloud infrastructure buildout and capital spending.** Oracle expects cloud and software expenses to keep rising as it adds data center capacity in existing and new regions. Delays in the buildout would affect its cloud revenue forecasts [ORCL chunk 212, chunk 146]. Its quarterly results may also swing with the timing of capital expenditures, which depend on supplier pricing, tariffs, and construction schedules [ORCL chunk 146].

5. **Earnings volatility.** Software license and hardware revenue is hard to forecast and tends to close late in each quarter. Because much of the cost base is fixed, revenue shortfalls hit profit disproportionately.
